title: DistilBERT: Smaller, Faster, Cheaper, Lighter
hook: Distill during pre-training instead of after, and you get a general-purpose language model that is 40% smaller and 60% faster while keeping 97% of BERT's understanding.
key_points: Applies knowledge distillation during pre-training to produce a general-purpose distilled language model.
40% smaller than BERT and runs 60% faster.
Trained with a triple loss: a language-modeling term, a distillation term, and a cosine-distance term.
content_html: Victor Sanh, Lysandre Debut, Julien Chaumond, and Thomas Wolf released DistilBERT in October 2019, showing that knowledge distillation can be applied during pre-training rather than only on a downstream task. The result is a general-purpose distilled language model that stays close to BERT's quality while being much lighter to run.
extra_html:
How it works

DistilBERT is trained against BERT during pre-training using a triple loss: a language-modeling term, a distillation term that pulls the student toward the teacher's outputs, and a cosine-distance term that aligns their hidden representations. Distilling at the pre-training stage means the resulting model is general-purpose, ready to fine-tune like BERT rather than tied to a single task.

Why it matters

The authors report that DistilBERT is 40% smaller than BERT and runs 60% faster, while retaining 97% of BERT's language understanding. That combination made it a popular default when teams needed BERT-like quality under tight latency or memory budgets, and a concrete demonstration of distillation applied to large language models.

related.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
related.hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.

related.title: BERT: Pretraining Deep Bidirectional Transformers
related.hook: What if a model read a sentence both directions at once? BERT did, by masking words and predicting them — and made pretrain-then-fine-tune the default recipe in NLP.
